description_detailed: Animals hold a special place in the hearts of the French. Companions in life, symbols of nature or sources of wonder, they incite deep affection and a sincere attachment. Some of them stand out for their popularity and the emotion they avoke. This selection celebrates France's favourite animals, those that touch and inspire us and reflect the strong bond we have with the animal world.In 2025, Monnaie de Paris wants to highlight French's favourite animals: cats, dogs, rabbits and horses. These 4 animals are also those that are particularly protected and welcomed by the Société Protectrice des Animaux, which is celebrating 180 years of commitment to the animal cause in 2025.Each coin in this series is much more than a collector's item: it embodies a universal message of compassion, a recognition of the daily work of the teams and volunteers, and an appeal to the collective conscience. Through this collection, the SPA and Monnaie de Paris wish to affirm their shared desire to raise public awareness of the animal cause, and to perpetuate the memory of a just struggle, driven by emotion, action and conviction. And what better way to pay tribute to your pet than to have it engraved on a coin?To celebrate the 180th anniversary of the Société Protectrice des Animaux, Monnaie de Paris is dedicating a new collection to the four favourite animals of the French: dogs, cats, rabbits and horses.This 250€ gold coin pay tribute to the millions of animals that have been taken in, cared for, protected and adopted thanks to the SPA's commitment since 1845, and engrave in the metal all the affection they have for them:The dog, a faithful companion, symbolises loyalty, daily presence and trust.The cat, an endearing companion, evokes mystery and independence.The rabbit, an affectionate companion, represents sensitivity and curiosity.The horse, majestic and sensitive, embodies strength and intelligence.Together on this coin, they pay tribute to the millions of animals rescued, cared for and loved thanks to the commitment of the SPA since 1845.
